description: AMD Infinity Context — GPU, vLLM, LMCache, NIXL/L2, NVMe, Node

panels.description: Cumulative completed inference requests since last metrics reset (all finish reasons: stop, length, abort, error).
panels.title: Total Prompts

panels.description: Cumulative prompt tokens processed since last metrics reset. Includes tokens served from GPU prefix cache, LMCache L1, LMCache L2, and full compute.
panels.title: Total Input Tokens

panels.description: Cumulative generation (decode) tokens produced since last metrics reset.
panels.title: Total Output Tokens

panels.description: Cumulative prompt tokens that required full GPU prefill — no cache hit at any tier. The expensive path; high values relative to total input tokens means low cache effectiveness.
panels.title: Tokens Computed (prefill)

panels.description: Cumulative prompt tokens served from the LMCache DRAM L1 cache. These bypassed GPU prefill entirely via the local_cache_hit path.
panels.title: Tokens from LMCache L1

panels.description: Cumulative prompt tokens served via external KV transfer from the LMCache L2 NVMe store (NIXL POSIX or AIS_MT). Non-zero confirms the L1→NVMe→GPU round-trip is working.
panels.title: Tokens from LMCache L2

panels.description: Average time to first token over the selected time window (sum of TTFT / request count). Dominated by prefill compute; low values confirm prefix cache hits are short-circuiting prefill.
panels.title: Avg TTFT

panels.description: Average time per output token (inter-token latency) over the selected time window — the per-step decode speed. High TPOT means decode is memory-bandwidth bound or the batch is too large.
panels.title: Avg TPOT

panels.description: Total token throughput: prompt tokens processed plus generation tokens produced per second. The primary inference throughput metric.
panels.title: Total Tokens/s

panels.description: Fraction of prompt tokens served from any cache tier (L1 + L2) vs total prompt tokens. = (local_cache_hit + external_kv_transfer) / prompt_tokens_total. 100% means zero prefill compute needed.
panels.title: Cache Hit Rate

panels.description: Fraction of prompt tokens served from LMCache L1 DRAM vs total prompt tokens. A high L1 rate means the DRAM cache is large enough to absorb most reuse without touching NVMe.
panels.title: L1 Hit Rate

panels.description: Fraction of prompt tokens served from LMCache L2 NVMe vs total prompt tokens. Non-zero confirms L2 reads are reaching vLLM. Low values vs L1 hit rate are expected (L1 absorbs most reuse; L2 handles overflow).
panels.title: L2 Hit Rate
GPU VRAM Used %

targets.expr: 100 * avg by (gpu_id, card_model) (gpu_used_vram{gpu_id=~"$gpu_id"}) / avg by (gpu_id, card_model) (gpu_total_vram{gpu_id=~"$gpu_id"})

panels.description: Percentage of GPU VRAM in use: gpu_used_vram / gpu_total_vram. High values risk OOM; vLLM targets ~90% via --gpu-memory-utilization.

panels.title: GPU VRAM Used (MB)
panels.description: Absolute GPU VRAM used and total capacity in MB. Used = active KV cache blocks + model weights + CUDA overhead.

panels.title: GPU Power (W)
panels.description: Average package power draw in watts. Sustained near TDP indicates the GPU is compute-bound.

panels.title: GPU System Clock (Hz)
panels.description: GPU system (shader) clock in Hz. Throttling below base clock indicates thermal or power-limit pressure.

panels.title: GPU Memory Temp (°C)
panels.description: GPU HBM memory temperature in °C. AMD throttles memory clocks above ~95°C.

panels.title: GPU Memory Clock (Hz)
panels.description: GPU memory (HBM) clock in Hz. Drops under thermal or power-limit throttle.

panels.title: Request Throughput (req/s)
panels.description: Completed inference requests per second across all finish reasons (stop / length). Throughput ceiling is set by model size, batch size, and KV cache availability.

panels.title: Time to First Token (s)
panels.description: Time from request arrival to first output token, p50 and p95. Dominated by prefill compute; a cold KV cache raises TTFT. Values near 0 indicate prefix cache hits short-circuiting prefill.

panels.title: Prompt Tokens by Source (rate)
panels.description: Prompt tokens broken down by how they were served each second: local_cache_hit (GPU prefix cache), external_kv_transfer (LMCache L2 fetch), and local_compute (full prefill). A healthy AIC run shows local_cache_hit or external_kv_transfer dominating.

panels.title: Requests Running / Waiting
panels.description: Active and queued inference requests. Sustained waiting > 0 means the engine is saturated; tune concurrency or reduce request rate.

panels.title: External Prefix Cache Queries vs Hits
panels.description: Rate of external prefix cache lookups vs confirmed hits. A high query rate with zero hits means the LMCache L2 is not returning blocks in time (check NIXL RX panel).

panels.title: L1 Usage
panels.description: LMCache DRAM L1 fill level (0–1). The L1 is intentionally sized to overflow into L2; values near 1 are expected and drive L2 writes.

panels.title: L1 Memory Used
panels.description: Raw DRAM bytes consumed by the LMCache L1 tensor store.

panels.title: L2 Usage
panels.description: Bytes written to the L2 NVMe/NFS store (NIXL POSIX or AIS_MT). Grows as L1 evictions push KV blocks to persistent storage.

panels.title: LMCache L1 Chunks (rate)
panels.description: Rate of KV chunk writes into and reads out of the LMCache DRAM L1. Read rate rising after a GPU cache reset confirms L2→L1 prefetch is working.

panels.title: L2 Store Requests (rate)
panels.description: L2 store requests submitted vs completed per second. A persistent gap indicates the NIXL write queue is backlogged (reduce --l2-prefetch-max-in-flight or increase POSIX slot size).

Net KV chunks added to the LMCache DRAM L1 over the selected time range (writes minus evictions). Rising during warmup, near-zero when L1 is full and evictions balance writes. A negative value means more evictions than writes — L1 is being drained (e.g. post-reset).
panels.title: L1 Live Chunks (writes − evictions)

panels.description: Cumulative KV chunks successfully written to and loaded back from the L2 NIXL store. The difference (stored − loaded) represents chunks in L2 that have not yet been prefetched back to L1. A growing loaded line after a GPU cache reset confirms L2 retrieval is working.
panels.title: L2 Chunks Stored vs Loaded
NIXL L2 Write Throughput (B/s)
panels.description: NIXL agent transmit throughput — bytes written to L2 NVMe/NFS storage per second. Peaks during warmup as the L1 overflows.

panels.title: NIXL L2 Read Throughput (B/s) — L2 Hit Signal
panels.description: NIXL agent receive throughput — bytes read back from L2 per second. This is the primary signal that L2 cache hits are occurring. Should go non-zero after a GPU prefix cache reset when anchor prompts are re-sent.

panels.title: NIXL Prefetch
panels.description: NIXL prefetch activity: lookup requests, confirmed hits, and in-flight prefetch jobs. Prefetch hit rate = hit chunks / lookup chunks; low rate means blocks are not in L2 yet or the prefetch window is too small.

panels.title: NVMe Throughput (B/s)
panels.description: NVMe read and write throughput in bytes/s for the selected device(s). LMCache NIXL writes appear here; sustained write bandwidth indicates active L2 fill.

panels.title: NVMe IOPS
panels.description: NVMe read and write IOPS. High read IOPS after a GPU cache reset confirms LMCache is retrieving KV blocks from NVMe.

panels.title: NVMe Average Latency (ms)
panels.description: Average NVMe read and write latency in ms (io_time / completions). Latencies above ~1 ms for reads indicate queue depth pressure or drive saturation.

panels.title: CPU Usage
panels.description: Host CPU utilization across all cores. High CPU during inference typically indicates LMCache serialization overhead or NIXL descriptor pool contention.

panels.title: Memory Used
panels.description: Host DRAM currently in use (MemTotal - MemAvailable). Includes GPU driver pinned memory and LMCache tensor allocations.

panels.title: Memory Total
panels.description: Total installed host DRAM.

panels.title: RDMA Port Throughput (B/s)
panels.description: RDMA port receive and transmit throughput in bytes/s. Active when LMCache is using NFS-over-RDMA for the L2b tier.

panels.title: hsa-snoop AIS Storage (rate)
panels.description: hsa-snoop AIS (AMD Infinity Storage) P2P byte throughput. TX = GPU writes to NVMe via hipFile P2PDMA; RX = NVMe reads back to GPU. Only non-zero when hsa-snoop is running with the AIS_MT NIXL backend active (not POSIX backend).

GPU kernel dispatch rate per second, broken down by kernel name and process (comm). Shows which kernels dominate dispatch bandwidth. vLLM::EngineCor launching attention + GEMM kernels is expected; a sudden drop to zero indicates the GPU is idle or a process has stalled.
panels.title: Kernel Launch Rate (launches/s by kernel)

panels.description: Total GPU kernel dispatch rate aggregated by process name (comm). Lets you see how launch bandwidth is split between vLLM engine cores, lmcache, and any other GPU processes. Each comm label corresponds to one GPU-using process group.
panels.title: Kernel Launch Rate by Process

panels.description: Number of active HSA AQL compute queues and SDMA queues currently open. Each vLLM worker thread typically holds one AQL queue. A drop to zero means no GPU process is running.
panels.title: Active AQL / SDMA Queues

panels.description: Rate of HSA barrier packets (synchronisation points) per process. Barriers are inserted between dependent GPU operations. A very high barrier rate relative to kernel launches suggests the workload is latency-bound on synchronisation rather than compute-bound.
panels.title: Barrier Packets (rate by process)

panels.description: p50 and p95 execution duration in milliseconds for the top dispatched kernels. Long-tail p95 values indicate occasional stalls (cache pressure, memory contention). The wvSplitK GEMM and kernel_unified_attention kernels dominate vLLM inference; their durations track batch size and sequence length.
panels.title: Kernel Duration p50 / p95 (top kernels, ms)

panels.description: SDMA (System DMA) engine operations: copy count rate and byte throughput per process. SDMA handles host↔device and device↔device memory transfers outside the compute queues. LMCache uses SDMA for KV tensor copies; high SDMA byte rate during L2 reads confirms data is moving from NVMe-backed host memory to GPU VRAM.
panels.title: SDMA Byte Throughput (B/s by process)

panels.description: SDMA DMA copy operation rate and total SDMA packet rate across all processes. Each copy op typically corresponds to one tensor transfer. Correlate with NIXL RX bytes — if NIXL RX rises but SDMA copies stay flat, the transfer path bypasses the SDMA engine (e.g. direct NVLink or P2PDMA).
panels.title: SDMA Copy & Packet Rate (ops/s)

panels.description: GFX (shader) activity, UMC (memory controller) activity, and MMA (matrix unit) utilisation from the AMD device-metrics-exporter. All three together show whether the GPU is compute-bound (high GFX), memory-bandwidth-bound (high UMC), or attention/GEMM-bound (high MMA). Expected during inference: high GFX+UMC, moderate MMA.
panels.title: GPU Compute / Memory / Matrix Activity (%)

panels.description: GPU edge temperature (package surface) and junction temperature (hottest die point). AMD throttles clocks when junction exceeds ~110°C on most Instinct cards. Monitor junction closely under sustained inference load.
panels.title: GPU Temperatures (°C)

panels.description: PCIe link speed in GT/s — confirms the GPU is running at its negotiated Gen4/Gen5 rate. A drop (e.g. Gen5→Gen3) indicates a slot or BIOS regression and will cap host↔GPU DMA bandwidth. xGMI shows inter-GPU fabric throughput on multi-GPU nodes.
panels.title: PCIe Speed / xGMI Fabric (GT/s)

panels.description: vLLM's GPU KV cache fill level. When this approaches 100%, new requests are queued and existing ones risk preemption. The AIC stack offloads KV blocks to LMCache when the GPU cache is full — watch this alongside the LMCache L1 write rate. Set via --gpu-memory-utilization.
panels.title: GPU KV Cache Usage %

panels.description: End-to-end request latency from receipt to last token delivered, p50 and p95. This is the user-facing SLO metric. Spikes on p95 relative to p50 indicate tail latency from KV cache misses, queue buildup, or preemptions.
panels.title: E2E Request Latency p50 / p95 (s)

panels.description: Time between consecutive output tokens, p50 and p95. ITL reflects decode throughput — high ITL means decode is bottlenecked (small batch, memory-bandwidth limited, or preemption stalls). A flat ITL under load confirms the engine is not falling behind.
panels.title: Inter-Token Latency p50 / p95 (s)

panels.description: vLLM's internal GPU-side prefix cache: queries and hits per second. This is distinct from the LMCache external KV transfer path — hits here bypass LMCache entirely and serve from GPU VRAM. A high hit rate reduces both TTFT and LMCache load.
panels.title: GPU Prefix Cache Hit Rate

panels.description: Request preemptions (KV cache evictions of in-flight requests — should be near zero) and p95 queue wait time. Rising preemptions mean the GPU KV cache is full and requests are being re-scheduled, causing latency spikes. Tune --gpu-memory-utilization or request rate.
panels.title: Preemptions & Queue Time p95

panels.description: vLLM's estimated FLOP rate and read/write memory bandwidth per GPU per second. Provides a rough GPU efficiency signal — compare against theoretical peak to estimate MFU (model FLOP utilisation). Both are estimates derived from the attention and GEMM kernel shapes.
panels.title: Estimated GPU FLOP & Memory Bandwidth Rate

panels.description: Throughput of KV blocks being loaded from the LMCache DRAM L1 back into GPU VRAM (the L0→L1 path in reverse). Peaks when vLLM retrieves cached blocks after an L1 hit. High sustained load throughput confirms the L1 cache is serving GPU prefill effectively.
panels.title: L1→GPU Load Throughput (GB/s)

panels.description: Number of L2 NIXL store operations currently in-flight. With the POSIX backend and max-gpu-workers=1, this should stay low (serialised writes). A growing queue means writes are accumulating faster than the NIXL backend can drain them — raise POST_WARMUP_SLEEP_S or reduce concurrent clients.
panels.title: L2 In-Flight Store Queue Depth

panels.description: Time between a KV chunk being stored and the next time it is reused, p50 and p95. A short reuse gap means the workload has high prompt reuse (good cache efficiency). A long gap or rising p95 indicates sparse reuse — the cache is filling with chunks that are rarely hit again.
panels.title: Chunk Reuse Gap (s) — Cache Effectiveness

panels.description: Rates of LMCache internal operations. prefetch requests = cache lookup operations initiated by vLLM; L2 store submitted = KV chunks being written to NVMe; L2 load submitted = NVMe prefetch reads back to L1.
panels.title: LMCache Operation Rate

panels.description: Throughput of KV tensor transfers between GPU (L0) and DRAM (L1). Store: GPU→DRAM (KV written to lmcache L1 after prefill). Load: DRAM→GPU (KV retrieved from L1 for reuse). Source: lmcache_mp_l0_l1_store/load_throughput_GB_per_second histograms.
panels.title: LMCache L0→L1 Throughput (GB/s)

panels.description: System load averages. A load sustained above CPU count ($(nproc)) indicates CPU saturation. During inference the CPU load is typically low; spikes suggest LMCache Python overhead, NIXL descriptor pool contention, or OS scheduler pressure.
panels.title: System Load (1m / 5m / 15m)

panels.description: Per-NVMe-device namespace used vs total capacity. The NIXL POSIX L2 backend writes slot files that grow as the cache fills. Running out of space silently stalls new L2 writes — monitor this to know when to increase NVME_DATA or reduce slot count.
panels.title: NVMe Capacity Used (bytes)

panels.description: Linux PSI (Pressure Stall Information) IO stall rate — fraction of time tasks are stalled waiting for I/O. A rising stall rate during L2 writes/reads means NVMe is saturated and blocking the LMCache NIXL write path. Correlate with NVMe latency panel.
panels.title: IO Pressure (PSI stalled seconds rate)

panels.description: Raw InfiniBand port receive and transmit throughput from the node-exporter infiniband collector. Complements the rdma-exporter panel with a different label set (device + port). Active when LMCache is using NFS-over-RDMA for the L2b tier.
panels.title: InfiniBand / RoCE Port Throughput (B/s)

panels.description: Available bytes on key mountpoints. Watch /mnt/lmcache-nvme (NIXL POSIX L2 slot files) and /mnt/lmcache-nfs (NFS L2b). Running either to zero will silently break new L2 writes without an error from LMCache.
panels.title: Filesystem Available Space
vLLM — ISL / OSL (Input & Output Sequence Length)

panels.description: Input sequence length distribution over time: p50, p95, and p99 of vllm:request_prompt_tokens. A widening spread between p50 and p99 indicates high variance in prompt lengths — common in mixed workloads. Rising p99 can explain tail TTFT spikes since longer prompts require more prefill compute.
panels.title: ISL Distribution (prompt tokens) — p50 / p95 / p99

panels.description: Output sequence length distribution over time: p50, p95, and p99 of vllm:request_generation_tokens. OSL is bounded by --max-tokens in the request. A low p50 with high p99 means most requests are short but a tail runs long — these long requests consume KV cache blocks for extended periods and increase preemption risk.
panels.title: OSL Distribution (generation tokens) — p50 / p95 / p99

panels.description: Mean input sequence length over the selected time range, computed as sum(rate(prompt_tokens_sum)) / sum(rate(prompt_tokens_count)). Reflects the typical prompt size hitting the model during this window.
panels.title: Average ISL (prompt tokens)

panels.description: Mean output sequence length over the selected time range, computed as sum(rate(generation_tokens_sum)) / sum(rate(generation_tokens_count)). Together with average ISL, determines the average total sequence length and therefore the average KV cache footprint per request.
panels.title: Average OSL (generation tokens)

panels.description: 99th percentile input sequence length over the selected time range. The worst-case prompt size driving tail TTFT and KV cache pressure.
panels.title: ISL p99 (prompt tokens)

panels.description: 99th percentile output sequence length over the selected time range. The worst-case generation length — long-running requests that hold KV cache blocks and risk preemption.
panels.title: OSL p99 (generation tokens)

panels.description: Average input and output sequence lengths plotted together. Useful for spotting correlation between prompt length and generation length, and for identifying when the workload shifts (e.g. shorter prompts during warmup vs longer prompts during the cliff benchmark). The ratio OSL/ISL is a rough proxy for how much new content is generated per cached token.
panels.title: Average ISL vs OSL over time

panels.description: Request completion rate and total token throughput (prompt + generation) per second. Provides workload intensity context for the ISL/OSL panels — a rising request rate with stable ISL/OSL means the load is scaling up without changing workload characteristics.
panels.title: Request Rate & Total Tokens/s

panels.description: Average GPU VRAM in use over the selected time window, across all selected GPU IDs. Includes model weights, KV cache blocks, and CUDA overhead. Expressed in bytes; divide by 1 GiB mentally for context against total VRAM shown in the GPU row.
panels.title: Avg GPU VRAM Used

panels.description: Average LMCache DRAM L1 bytes in use over the selected time window. Reflects how full the L1 tier has been on average — near the L1 cap confirms steady overflow to L2.
panels.title: Avg LMCache L1 Used

panels.description: Average LMCache L2 NVMe bytes in use over the selected time window. Grows as L1 evictions write KV chunks to the NIXL POSIX or AIS_MT backend. A stable non-zero value confirms the L2 tier is populated and serving reads.
panels.title: Avg LMCache L2 Used

panels.description: 1 when the LMCache MP coordinator /healthz returns healthy; 0 when unreachable.
panels.title: Coordinator Up

panels.description: Number of LMCache MP server instances currently registered with the coordinator.
panels.title: Registered Instances

panels.description: Sum across all instances of lmcache_coordinator_instance_seq_gap. Non-zero means at least one MP server had an event-stream sequence gap — the key directory may have missed some placements.
panels.title: Event Stream Gaps

panels.description: Keys with at least one placement tracked in the coordinator key directory. Growth indicates active KV block advertising from MP servers.
panels.title: Key Directory — Keys & Placements

panels.description: L1 keys reported by each MP server's event stream to the coordinator key directory. Separate lines per instance_id.
panels.title: L1 Keys per Instance

panels.description: KV chunk keys in the coordinator key directory by tier. L1 keys: chunks currently held in DRAM across all instances. L2 keys (derived): directory_keys_total − L1 keys = chunks evicted to NVMe.
panels.title: Coordinator Key Directory

panels.description: Time the coordinator exporter takes to scrape all REST endpoints. Spikes indicate coordinator slowness or network latency.
panels.title: Coordinator Exporter Scrape Latency (s)

panels.description: Active vs draining L2 store/prefetch adapters. An adapter enters 'draining' when lmcache shuts down or a NIXL init error forces the adapter offline. Sustained draining=1 with active=0 indicates a nixl_posix pool init failure (e.g. stale pool files from a previous run).
panels.title: L2 Adapter State (active vs draining)

panels.description: Average NIXL transfer latency per request = agent_xfer_time_total / agent_tx_requests_num_total. agent_xfer_time_total is in microseconds (Start-to-Complete per request). High values indicate NVMe saturation or NIXL registration overhead.
panels.title: NIXL Average Transfer Latency (µs/req)

panels.description: L1 allocation failures (lmcache_mp_l1_allocation_failure_total) indicate L1 is full and chunks are being dropped rather than stored — increase L1 size. Eviction loop triggered (lmcache_mp_l1_eviction_loop_triggered_total) shows when LRU eviction fires above the watermark.
panels.title: L1 Allocation Failures & Eviction Triggers (rate)

panels.description: Total number of KV cache blocks that fit in GPU VRAM at the current gpu_memory_utilization setting. Each block holds block_size tokens (currently 64) across all layers. Read from vllm:cache_config_info num_gpu_blocks label. Static — changes only on vLLM restart.
panels.title: VRAM KV Cache Block Capacity

panels.description: Live KV chunks currently held in LMCache DRAM L1 = writes minus evictions.
panels.title: KV Chunks in L1

panels.description: KV chunks stored in LMCache L2 NVMe (cumulative stored minus evicted). Proxy for current L2 occupancy; resets on lmcache restart.
panels.title: KV Chunks in L2

panels.description: KV cache block lifetime: time from allocation to eviction. p50/p95 from both vLLM's sampled block tracking (5% sample rate) and lmcache's L0 (GPU) block tracking. Short lifetimes under load indicate KV cache pressure; longer lifetimes mean the prefix cache is stable.
panels.title: KV Block Lifetime p50/p95 (s)

panels.description: Time a KV block spent idle (unreferenced) before being evicted. High idle time = blocks held in the prefix cache for a long time before eviction, which is good (warm cache). Low idle time = blocks evicted almost immediately, indicating cache thrashing under memory pressure.
panels.title: KV Block Idle Before Eviction p50/p95 (s)

panels.description: Time between successive reuses of the same KV block/chunk. vLLM: sampled GPU block reuse gaps (5% sample). lmcache L1: gaps between touches of the same L1 DRAM chunk. NaN/absent = no reuse events yet in this window — send repeated prompts to populate.
panels.title: KV Block Reuse Gap p50/p95 (s)

panels.description: GPU↔DRAM KV tensor transfer throughput from lmcache's L0 store/load histograms. Store = GPU→DRAM (writing KV to lmcache L1 after prefill). Load = DRAM→GPU (retrieving KV from lmcache L1 for cache hits). Complements the NIXL L2 throughput panels above.
panels.title: L0→L1 KV Transfer Throughput p50 (B/s)

panels.description: GPU-side prefix cache hit rate over time (rate over $__rate_interval). Complements the summary stat panel. Shows how cache warmth evolves across a session — rising rate = longer shared prefixes being served from VRAM without recompute.
panels.title: GPU Prefix Cache Hit Rate Over Time

title: AIC Overview
